name: Kurseong Tourist Lodge (WBTDC)
image_query: Kurseong Tourist Lodge Hill Cart Road
summary: The West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation's lodge on Hill Cart Road, about 1 km from Kurseong station. Sixteen double rooms, a restaurant and a momo corner where the toy train passes a few metres from your table.
body: The Kurseong Tourist Lodge is one of the government lodges that have stayed useful for decades because of where they stand. It sits on the main Hill Cart Road above the town, with the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway track running right outside, so the toy train rattles past the restaurant windows when it runs. Rooms are plain and clean rather than stylish, with attached baths, geysers and views down the valley from the better side.

It suits families and older travellers who want a known name, a restaurant on site and no surprises. Book through the WBTDC website or office, and ask for a valley-facing room. Even if you stay elsewhere, the momo corner is a fine place for lunch and a cup of tea while you wait for the train. Rates change by season; check current status before you travel.
why: Toy-train track right outside the restaurant
Walkable to Kurseong station and bazaar

faqs.q: How do I book the Kurseong Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Book through the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation's online booking or its offices in Kolkata and Siliguri. Weekends in April, May, October and the Puja holidays fill early, so book a month or more ahead for those dates. Midweek rooms in winter and the monsoon are usually easy to find a few days out.

faqs.q: Can I see the toy train from the lodge?
faqs.a: Yes. The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway runs along Hill Cart Road right beside the lodge, and the restaurant and momo corner look onto the track. Trains through Kurseong depend on the current timetable and on landslide repairs lower down, so ask at reception which services are running that day.

faqs.q: Is the lodge within walking distance of the town?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 1 km from Kurseong station and the main bazaar along Hill Cart Road, roughly a 15-minute walk. The road has jeep and car traffic and patchy footpaths, so take care at bends, and carry a torch if you walk back after dark.

name: Cochrane Place
summary: A restored colonial-era house on the Pankhabari road below Kurseong, run as a small heritage hotel with tea-garden views. Our one splurge suggestion in this land: more expensive than a homestay, but far less than Darjeeling's big heritage hotels.
body: Cochrane Place stands on the Pankhabari road below Kurseong town, with tea slopes falling away towards the plains. The hotel is built around an old hill house, its rooms are furnished in a period style, and the terraces look across the tea slopes of the valley towards the plains. Ask the hotel directly about meals, tea tastings and garden walks, as what is offered changes with the season.

We include it for travellers on our Comfort journeys and for couples who want one special night in the middle of a budget trip. It is a short drive to Makaibari and about 10–15 minutes to Kurseong bazaar. Prices vary widely by room and season, so compare directly with the hotel and check current status before you travel.
why: Short drive to Makaibari and Kurseong
A one-night splurge that still costs less than Darjeeling's grand hotels

faqs.q: Is Cochrane Place a budget hotel?
faqs.a: No. It is a mid-to-upper-range heritage hotel, usually ₹6,000–11,000 a room depending on room and season. We suggest it as a single splurge night on a Comfort or honeymoon trip. For a budget stay in the same valley, the Makaibari village homestays cost far less and include meals.

faqs.q: How far is Cochrane Place from Kurseong town?
faqs.a: It is on the Pankhabari road below Kurseong, about 10–15 minutes by car from the bazaar and station. Walking up is possible but steep. Shared jeeps on the Pankhabari road pass by and cost very little; the hotel can also arrange a car for pick-up from Siliguri.

faqs.q: Can I visit Makaibari from Cochrane Place?
faqs.a: Yes. Makaibari's factory and village area are a short drive from the hotel on the same Pankhabari road. Factory visits depend on the season and the day's work, so ask the hotel or the estate a day ahead. March to November is the plucking season.

name: Makaibari village homestays
summary: The Makaibari estate's homestay programme places guests with tea workers' families in the villages on the estate. You get a simple room, home-cooked meals and a walk through the gardens, and your money goes straight to the household.
body: Makaibari started its homestay arrangement with the workers' villages on the estate years before 'homestay' became a travel buzzword. Families who join keep a clean room or two for guests, cook dinner and breakfast, and often walk you to the plucking sections or the factory. Rooms are simple: a bed with heavy quilts, an attached or shared bathroom depending on the house, and hot water in a bucket in some homes.

This is the stay for travellers who want to understand how a tea garden works from the inside. Expect dal, rice, local greens, squash and pickles, and tea at any hour. Book through the estate or a Kurseong contact you trust, and confirm the rate, the meals and the bathroom type in advance.
why: Sleep with a tea worker's family inside a working estate
Meals and garden walks included in a low price
Money goes directly to the host household

faqs.q: How much do the Makaibari homestays cost?
faqs.a: Expect roughly ₹1,500–2,000 per person per night with dinner and breakfast, as a 2025–26 indication. The rate depends on the house, the room and whether the bathroom is attached. Confirm the price and what is included before you go, and pay the family directly.

faqs.q: How do I book a Makaibari homestay?
faqs.a: Contact the estate or a homestay coordinator in Makaibari village; Kurseong hotels and drivers can also put you in touch. Give your dates and the number of guests, and ask for an attached bathroom if you need one. Book further ahead for the first flush in March and April and for October.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Makaibari factory while staying there?
faqs.a: Usually yes, during the plucking season from March to November, but it depends on the day's work. Your host can often arrange a walk to the factory or the plucking sections. Tastings at the estate may have a fee; ask about the cost before you start.

name: Mirik Swiss Cottages (GTA)
summary: Duplex cottages run by the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration on the high ground above Sumendu Lake. Old-fashioned government lodging with a view of the lake and the town, a short walk down to the water.
body: The Swiss Cottages are one of Mirik's government properties, built as a cluster of duplex cottages on the hill above the lake. Today they come under the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration's tourism department. The appeal is the location: you look down over Sumendu Lake and Krishnanagar, and you are a short walk from the lake path and the road up to Bokar Monastery.

Expect plain government-lodge furnishings, upstairs bedrooms and simple food from the property kitchen or the lake-side restaurants. It suits families who want space and a quiet hill above the day-trip crowds. Booking methods and rates change; check current status with the GTA tourism office before you travel.
why: Duplex cottages with room for families
Walking distance to the lake path and Bokar Monastery road

faqs.q: Who runs the Swiss Cottages in Mirik?
faqs.a: They are run by the tourism department of the Gorkhaland Territorial Administration, the body that manages tourism properties in the Darjeeling hills. Booking channels have changed over the years, so contact the GTA tourism office in Darjeeling or Siliguri, or a trusted local agent, to book and confirm current rates.

faqs.q: How far are the Swiss Cottages from Mirik lake?
faqs.a: They stand on the high ground above the lake, a short downhill walk of about 10 minutes to the lake path and footbridge. The return is uphill, which older guests may prefer to do by car. Bokar Monastery is a further drive or a 30–40 minute uphill walk.

faqs.q: Are the Swiss Cottages good for a family?
faqs.a: Yes. The duplex layout gives separate space for a family, and the hill is quieter than the lake-side hotels in Krishnanagar. Facilities are basic government-lodge standard, so ask about heaters in winter and hot water before you book, and carry snacks for children.
